analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bayern are top on goal difference and unbeaten in the league, but Vincent Kompany is still recovering at home from meningeal irritation (assistant Aaron Danks has led the team since late October) and Manuel Neuer went off at half-time in Mainz with a foot problem, so Jonas Urbig is likely in goal. Köln have won one of their last seven league games and lost the Rhine derby; with Thijs Dallinga out for the season and Ragnar Ache a doubt, their threat leans on Saïd El Mala. Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz are both training again and could return here.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.5 goals, with 3.7 for Bayern. I lean a little lower: Köln have scored only 10 in nine games and are without Dallinga, so 0.8 for them looks generous, and Bayern's first game back after an international break, with Kompany's return still open, may not be at full speed. Bayern should still clear three at home.

corners.text: The site expects 10.9 corners, 7.2 of them Bayern's. I lean slightly higher: Bayern had about 81% of the ball in Mainz and Köln, short of a target man, are likely to sit deep and clear crosses behind. Michael Olise drives at defenders from wide all game, and a returning Díaz would add another winger.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean higher because Köln collected six yellow cards in the derby against Leverkusen and seven were shown in their 1-1 at Union, a pattern of chasing and fouling that fits an evening spent without the ball in Munich. Bayern rarely take more than one or two, and the referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The site has 32 shots, 21.8 for Bayern and 10.3 for Köln. Bayern's part fits their season (184 shots in their first eight games, about 23 per game), but ten for Köln at the Allianz Arena looks high for a side that managed ten at home in the derby and has lost its main striker. I lean a touch lower overall.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.5 on target, 9.3 from Bayern. Bayern had seven on target by the 72nd minute in Mainz, so their share is reasonable, but Köln's 3.2 looks generous given their blunt attack without Dallinga. I lean slightly lower, mostly on the Köln side.
